> This is the first-ever hardware project that I will be making! I am using an Arduino Uno R3, some LEDs, a Breadboard, resistors, and an ultrasonic sensor. I am making a sensor detection system that can be implemented in real life for sidewalks where there are traffic lights. The traffic lights will be red, yellow, or green according to the ultrasonic sensor. If the ultra sonic sensor detects something  coming towards the crosswalk(human) that is 21 cm or more away(for this model), it will turn the traffic light yellow. If the object is 20 or less cm away then it would make the light red. If there is no one then the light is green.

### 2026-10-03 — GOT MY ULTRASONIC SENSOR WORKING!

**2.1h**

GOT MY ULTRASONIC SENSOR WORKING!

Saturday October 3:

I started off getting my materials:
      1. Breadboard from the ELEGO Starter R3 kit
      2.  Arduino Uno R3 Board
     3.  Jumper Wires:  (Male to Male), (Female to Male)
     4.   Ultrasonic Sensor
      5. Breadboard(for LED)

### 2026-10-04 — Oct 3-  8:00 PM to 11:30 PM

**4.7h**

Oct 3-  8:00 PM to 11:30 PM

After adding the UltraSonic Sensor, I wanted to add the LCD display. However, I realised a little late that there is only one 5v pin on the arduino board. So I had to rewire the whole part again. I fixed tihs problem by putting one red wire from the 5V to thd positive side of the breadboard. This way I could conenct mutiple componets easily. SInce it was my first time using an LCD, I first thought about which type of LCD I should. I had a few round circle LCDs, and the common 16x2 LCD display. After researchging through google, and watching some yourube videos that explained the difference (Like Mr.Volt). I also researched through some websites: https://www.caisonlcd.com/blog/what-is-the-difference-between-round-and-rectangular-lcd-displays

This took me aroudn 1 hour and 30 minutes:, here are some pcitrues of researching:

![11113](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/bd1746a8431b2f035b31ab25adce51fa5dec11be527157931545ca13db5d7e5c.png)

Eventually I choose the Rectangle LCD disaply since it was easier for wiring, and disaplying text. The main differences between a round LCD and Rectangle LCD was that Round LCD's are more commonyl used for images, and need multiple libarieis to be installed.

Next I took a potentiometer and took some notes on it (some of these hardware pieces are new to me).

After placing it, I decided to learn more specifically about the Rectangle LCD:

Here's what I learned:

            1.  Vss is for GND(negative power)
            2. VDD is for 5v(positve power on the breadboard)
            3.   Vo( controls the contrast, RS, and other pins are used for different tasks)

Here is my program working after I coded it:

Basically my program works like this:

UltraSonic Sensor - If the sensor detects my hand  closer than 15 cm, then the LED turns red. If more than 15 cm but less than 25 cm, the LED turns yellow. If farther than 25 cm then LED turns green.

LCD- Based on the color of the LED the LCD dispalys different text

![62a81603-8a04-4e46-a893-6d111d96fa9d](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/d6aac402d71da5a537c925722d1f91845abb9f306fb40d8abeb7d4d344e7b8c8.jpeg)

In this image it also shows an IR sensor. After testing the code, I realised how do i know if the Ultra Sonic Sensor is working? To solve that, I added a IR sensor,and coded it quickly. I know a lot about IR sensors already, so it was easy to code it. All i had to do what print out the values for 0 or 1 on Serial Monitor. I tested my code to mke sure when the Ultr SOnic Sensor is showing a value less than 25 cm, then the Ir sensor should also be showing Value 0(in this case i tested first to see which vlaue shows my hand since it varies). After some trial and error, I decided this was good enough.
